fixture_name: Ramp-terminal arterial reconstruction — US preliminary design (MassDOT HSIP municipal RSA, full package)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Addresses substantive preliminary-design-stage hazards—undelineated ramp crossings without accessible ramps, vegetation-limited sightlines, a four-lane high-speed mid-block crossing with non-compliant signage and a prior fatality—all fixable before design freeze.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Site facts (missing crosswalks, vegetation, signage deficiency, fatal collision) are recorded input facts per Safety Issue #4, and verbatim quotes EV-US-030/EV-US-032 directly support the pivotal separation-failure mechanism and treatment duty, meeting the 2-level requirement.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed as a safety concern consistent with FHWA RSA semantics; MUTCD/ADA references function as remedial specificity within the safety argument rather than misfiled compliance questions.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Multi-part, phased, and actionable: immediate signage retrofit, ADA ramps and designated crossings in current design, future signalized ramp crossings, and relocation to Derby Shoppes signal via sidewalk extension—specific and viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians identified as the directly exposed vulnerable group with driver attention-diversion explicitly considered; impacts on both user classes are analyzed throughout the concern and recommendation.

justifications.substance: Undefined lane drop with abrupt striping termination, no advance warning, and late merging at a ramp mouth is a classic expectancy/decision-load failure mode with genuine crash potential between merging and turning drivers; squarely substantive for a preliminary-design-stage RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-033 supplies a verbatim quote directly supporting the pivotal claim (striping ends abruptly, no signage), satisfying the quote requirement; the observed late-merge behavior rests on recorded Safety Issue #2 field observations rather than a second direct quote, but the core concern is fully grounded.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a design/operational safety concern consistent with the FHWA RSA purpose quote (EV-US-023); no MUTCD or other compliance claim is asserted, keeping safety and compliance categorically distinct.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: advance merge signing and pavement markings ahead of the on-ramp, plus a viable design alternative (extend two through lanes past the ramp entrance with mandatory-right-turn trade-off signed in advance) appropriately fed into the ongoing reconstruction.
justifications.vru_coverage: Although the conflict mechanism is driver-to-driver, the finding explicitly identifies the adjacent mid-block crosswalk, recognizes the lane-drop attention-diversion effect on pedestrians, and properly delegates detailed VRU treatment to companion finding JB-GF12-001, demonstrating active consideration where relevant.
